summary: Changes the message type number for the Terminal Endpoint Identifier Query Request in the ISDN IUA protocol, because the old number clashed with one used by the DUA extension. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Two IUA-related messages had the same type number, so receivers could not distinguish them. This RFC changes the TEI Query Request type to 8.

questions: what is the iua tei query message type
why did rfc 5133 change message type 5 to 8
why did the tei query type change
subtitle: Changes the IUA TEI Query Request message type from 5 to 8.

tldr.problem: RFC 4233 assigned type 5 to TEI Query Request, which was already used for a DUA DLC Status message.
tldr.mechanism: TEI Query messages MUST use message type 8 instead of 5, and IANA reserved type 8 for them.
tldr.outcome: The change updates RFC 4233 and separates the TEI Query Request from the conflicting message type.

today: RFC 5133 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4233. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Message-Type Conflict
sections.content:
RFC 4233 introduced a Terminal Endpoint Identifier (TEI) Query Request using message type 5. The DUA extension in RFC 4129 had already assigned message types 5, 6, and 7 to Data Link Connection Status messages.

Using type 5 for both a DLC Status request and a TEI Query Request made them impossible to distinguish.
sections.plainLanguage: The same number identified two different messages. A receiver could not tell which message type 5 meant.

sections.title: The New TEI Query Type
sections.content:
This document updates RFC 4233: TEI Query messages MUST be encoded with message type 8 instead of 5.

No other message-type change is specified by this RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: TEI Query messages now use type 8. Type 5 remains available for the DUA message that already used it.

sections.title: Registry and Security
sections.content:
IANA reserved management message type 8 for TEI Query Request messages in the Signaling User Adaptation Layer Assignments registry.

The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those in RFC 4233.
sections.plainLanguage: The official registry now assigns type 8 to TEI Query Request. The RFC says it adds no new security considerations.
